accident_report:
Vehicle Initialization
On a three-lane one-way roadway at night with a dry surface and a wide shoulder on the right, three vehicles are traveling through a gentle left-hand curve. V1 is in lane 2, positioned slightly ahead of the others, moving at 80 km/h with steady throttle, intending to maintain its lane through the curve. V2 is in lane 2 behind V1 at a following distance of approximately 25 meters, traveling at 78 km/h, maintaining a safe following behavior and intending to keep coordinated speed with V1. V3 is in lane 1 (rightmost lane), slightly behind V2 by 10 meters, traveling at 82 km/h, intending to gradually overtake slower traffic while staying within its lane. All vehicles are in normal operating condition, with no aggressive maneuvers.

Scenario Development
As the vehicles enter the curved հատված of the roadway, the limited nighttime visibility reduces the drivers’ forward perception distance, even though the road is dry and friction is adequate. V1 slightly reduces speed from 80 km/h to 72 km/h to comfortably negotiate the curve while maintaining lane stability. This deceleration is smooth but occurs earlier than V2 anticipates due to reduced visibility around the bend. V2, maintaining coordinated speed and a safe following distance, begins a gentle deceleration from 78 km/h to 70 km/h in response to V1’s behavior. However, the curvature and darkness make V2’s perception of V1’s speed change slightly delayed, causing a shorter-than-expected headway momentarily.

Meanwhile, V3 in lane 1 continues at 82 km/h and begins to draw closer to V2. Observing V2’s deceleration, V3 decides to maintain its speed to pass, but due to the curve and limited sight distance, V3 underestimates how much V2 will slow. As V3 approaches the rear-right of V2, V2 further adjusts speed down to 68 km/h to re-establish a safe following distance behind V1, which is now steady at 72 km/h. This additional deceleration creates a closing speed difference between V3 and V2.

V3, now only about 8 meters behind V2 laterally offset in lane 1, initiates a mild deceleration from 82 km/h to 74 km/h. However, because of the curve geometry and reduced nighttime visibility, V3’s driver misjudges the lateral alignment and the relative motion of V2. Simultaneously, V2, aiming to maintain smooth traffic flow and speed coordination with V1, makes a slight leftward lane-centering adjustment within lane 2, bringing it marginally closer to the lane boundary.

Result
Due to the combined effects of the curve, nighttime visibility limitations, and speed coordination adjustments, V3’s front-left corner makes contact with V2’s rear-right corner at approximately 72 km/h versus 68 km/h. This constitutes the first collision in the scenario, involving V2 and V3, triggered by the interaction between coordinated deceleration, limited visibility in a curved հատված, and insufficient lateral and longitudinal clearance during the passing maneuver.
